What is your current agent workflow with TDD? Curious how to make mine better.

It depends on the task and the codebase I'm working in.

[ol:1]- If it's a codebase with good design, prompt llm to write acceptance tests for the behaviour I want. See them fail. Ask for implementation to pass the tests. Add more tests/refactor either with code/LLM depending on implementation.- If it's a bad codebase, figure a test/command to check something works. Prompt for characterisation tests, then figure out if first approach is worth it, or current is "good enough".- If I'm one shotting/vibe coding, I'll ask for tests as I go through testing the idea. I'll spend a decent amount of time helping the LLM make better app/test design for faster feedback so we can run the tests after each change.

How it worked: A whole lot of C++ code to power the simulation and graphics engines, and an art team to develop 3D models of any and every vehicle, aircraft, carrier, etc. that exists. Packaged up as an off-the-shelf desktop app, simulations were set up and run through the GUI with the option to hook up to a VR headset and go first person mode into the simulations (this was a popular use case for training contracts).

DraftKings: Everything written in C#/.NET for the backend, mobile was using React Native I believe but has been migrating to Xamarin so that they use the same stack throughout. Systems are very event-driven, hundreds of microservices, Kubernetes for auto scaling, everything hosted on AWS. Observability was half the job there, minutes of downtime would typically cost us millions of dollars lol. It was a cool gig but that part of it was high-stress for sure. Week 1 of NFL they would fly people out for the week just so issues could be resolved in person, probably saves them a lot of money in the end which is wild to think about 🤯
